public_rationale: This is sweeping rhetoric with no measure. It is unclear whether 'it' means generative AI as a whole or the effort to automate people away, and 'work' has no threshold. Klarna shows the problem. In 2024 it said its AI assistant did the work of 700 agents, which some would call a sign of it working. By May 2025 its CEO said the AI gave lower-quality output and the company was rehiring humans, which others would call failure. Which way this goes depends on a standard the speaker did not give, so I do not score it.
limitations: One company example is context only, not a survey of deployments.
